claims.text: For each package the script lists .dart files under lib/ with a line starting import/export naming 'package:<name>/, drops lib/l10n/ (written by gen-l10n), prints the file names when the count is 1-3, and sorts by count descending then name.

Stage-4 output: flutter (SDK) 20, flutter_riverpod 16, go_router 6, http 3 (keycloak_sign_in.dart, orders_api.dart, api_client.dart), web 2 (both browser_web.dart), crypto 1, flutter_web_plugins 1, cupertino_icons/flutter_localizations/intl 0.
The 16 lib/ files importing flutter_riverpod are in all three features (auth 3, catalog 4, ordering 6) plus main.dart, router.dart and shared/local_store.dart.
BrowserLocalStore implements the app's LocalStore with one web.window.localStorage call per method (getItem, setItem, removeItem); the rest of the app does not import package:web.

claims.text: shared/browser.dart exports browser_web.dart when dart.library.js_interop is available (holds when built for the browser) and browser_stub.dart otherwise; both define createLocalStore(), the stub's returning an in-memory MemoryLocalStore.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.App/lib/shared/browser.dart line 4, browser_stub.dart lines 3-5 @ stage-4; dart.dev conditional imports/exports

claims.text: Six files under DonHang.App/test import flutter_riverpod and give providers fixed values through overrides (ProviderScope or ProviderContainer); no file in test/ imports package:web; storage tests override localStoreProvider (the provider of LocalStore) with a MemoryLocalStore.
Riverpod screens read providers with ref.watch, which rebuilds the widget when the provider changes, and tests replace a provider's value with ProviderScope(overrides: [...]).
claims.source_hint: riverpod.dev docs: Reading providers (ref.watch); Testing (overrides); frontend.l2.riverpod-providers, frontend.l2.overriding-providers-in-tests

claims.text: A state library decides how every screen reads and changes data, so choosing one is a whole-app decision, judged by testing with overrides, how changes reach screens, and team knowledge, not popularity.

Wrapping a library pays off when it does one narrow job (web, two files, already two implementations); hiding Riverpod would mean copying ref.watch and overrides, a state library of the app's own, so DonHang.App accepts its reach.

An app-wide library is best replaced one feature per pull request with old and new both in pubspec.yaml until the last feature moves; a single change across all features conflicts with other work on those files while it is open.
A library imported by one file can be used directly; a wrapper would cost more than it saves. A second state library for one screen is still an app-wide choice.
